answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token stake before voting, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled, independently verified task exposes duplicate identities. The vote is weighted by stake rather than account count, so creating a plume of cheap wallets does not buy extra influence. An attacker must acquire and lock real capital for each identity, keep it unavailable during review, and risk losing it; a glacier of dormant accounts is costly too. A prism of verification checks makes evasion harder without treating one proof as infallible.
